Fiber orientation relative to B0 and DTI metrics

NIBS observational sanity check · generated 2026-09-28 · pipeline: extract_b0_pose.py → b0_tractometry.py → run_b0_analysis.py

Key findings

  • Design. Within-subject comparison of the two NIBS sessions: 22 participants, 71,304 paired bundle nodes. Natural head-pose changes between sessions had a median of 2.7° (the "manipulation").
  • Positive control (R2*). Within-subject β = 6 s⁻¹ per unit sin⁴θ (95% CI 4.02 to 7.71, permutation p = 2.0e-04); cross-sectional pose-isolated β = 4.03 (p = 1.0e-03). The pipeline does recover the known R2* orientation effect.
  • Primary result (FA). β = 0.00554 per unit sin⁴θ (95% bootstrap CI -0.0255 to 0.0404; pose-permutation p = 0.718). A β of 0.00554 means FA would differ by 0.00554 between a fiber parallel and perpendicular to B0 (extrapolated from small angle changes).
  • Comparison with the reference study. Kleban et al. (2023) tract-segment estimate at TE ≈ 88 ms: 0.061 [0.034, 0.088] FA per unit sin⁴θ. The NIBS 95% CI does not contain that estimate and overlaps its interval. Design-based power to detect the reference estimate was 95%. The reference used much stricter single-fiber voxels, so its effect is an upper bound on what these nodes should show (see Section 4).
  • Sensitivity/power. Minimal detectable |β| (80% power) is 0.0473 FA per unit sin⁴θ. The typical between-session Δ sin⁴θ at a node has SD 0.0206, so the within-subject signal would be about 0.00125 FA at the reference β and is about 1.14e-04 FA at the observed β, versus node-level test–retest noise SD ≈ 0.0188 FA.
  • Methodological caveat. A naive between-session Δ sin⁴θ gives FA β = -0.0177, but its pose-permutation null is centered at -0.0182 (p = 0.578): that slope comes from session-to-session changes in the estimated fiber orientation, not head pose. All primary estimates use the pose-isolated Δ sin⁴θ.
  • Secondary tensor metrics. AD β = 2.5 (95% CI -85.6 to 108, p = 0.961), RD β = -19.7 (95% CI -70.2 to 46.5, p = 0.516). Neither is distinguishable from zero.

Observational: head pose was not assigned. Estimates bound feasibility and effect size; they do not establish that B0 orientation causes FA differences.

Pre-specified inclusion: bundle not in the ICC exclusion list; group-average inner-shell FA ≥ 0.25; ≥ 20 streamlines; nodes 5–44 of 0–49; MSMT second/first fixel amplitude ratio < 0.5. Criteria do not use subject-level FA. Within-subject rows require inclusion in both sessions.

2. Head pose (feasibility gate)

B0 is the scanner z-axis (all runs head-first supine), expressed in each participant's ACPC space via rigid registration of the raw DWI b0 to the preprocessed reference (AP/PA averaged). The anatomical-chain estimate (QSIPrep MPRAGE transforms) is a cross-check and is used for MEGRE.

3. Leverage and anatomy

Only the change in sin⁴θ between sessions informs the within-subject estimate. Its distribution, and where in the bundles it is largest, are shown below. Along-tract profiles show how strongly FA and the anatomical fiber angle co-vary along bundles — the confound that a pooled correlation would mistake for a B0 effect.

4. Positive control and primary result

Model (plan §9, with pose isolation): Δy ~ β·Δfpose + γ·Δfest with participant × bundle fixed effects and f(θ) = sin⁴θ, where Δfpose = f(M̄, b₂) − f(M̄, b₁) changes only through head pose (M̄: two-session mean of the node's fiber-orientation moments; b: session B0) and Δfest = f(M₂, b̄) − f(M₁, b̄) captures session-to-session change in the estimated fiber orientation. Inference: cluster bootstrap over participants (5000 resamples) and a pose-permutation null that reassigns participants' pairs of B0 vectors (5000 permutations), keeping each participant's anatomy and measurements.

Why pose isolation is needed

The naive predictor f(M₂, b₂) − f(M₁, b₁) also varies with orientation-estimate changes between sessions, which track tractography/noise differences that also change FA. Its permutation null is therefore centered on the observed slope, not on zero: the naive "effect" is not attributable to head pose. The pose-isolated predictor removes this (null centered near 0).

The reference selected single-fiber voxels with a second/first peak ratio below 0.1 and low dispersion; NIBS nodes average over streamlines (median within-node dispersion 23.5°), and dispersion reduces the expected effect. Pose error also attenuates β. The reference estimate is therefore an upper bound on the slope expected here.

5. Cross-sectional, pose-isolated analysis

Model (plan §10), per session: y ~ sin⁴θ + sin⁴θ_ref with bundle × node and participant × bundle fixed effects. sin⁴θ_ref uses the group-mean B0 and absorbs anatomical orientation, so the sin⁴θ coefficient is identified by head pose only. CIs: cluster-robust (CR1) by participant; p: permutation of B0 across participants. The naive model omits sin⁴θ_ref.

7. Descriptive pooled relationship

Pooled plots mix anatomy with orientation and are not evidence for a B0 effect.

8. Methods summary and limitations

  • Tractometry: DSI Studio AutoTrack (MSMT) bundles in ACPC space; up to 1,000 streamlines per bundle resampled to 50 nodes; Gaussian Mahalanobis node weights; node order aligned across sessions and participants by centroid profiles.
  • Fiber direction (primary): at each streamline point, the MSMT-CSD fixel (QSIRecon fib) best aligned with the local tangent; sin⁴θ averaged over points per node (exactly, from second- and fourth-order orientation moments; not computed from a mean direction).
  • Participant-level covariates (change in bore position, change in mean motion) are constant within participant and are absorbed by the fixed effects of the differenced model.
  • Outcomes: TORTOISE inner-shell tensor (b ≤ 1200; primary); full-shell tensor and DKI as sensitivity; R2* (MEGRE, 5 echoes) sampled via rigid sMRIPrep-T1w→ACPC registration.
  • R2* pose uses the same-session anatomical-chain transform (MEGRE registration to T1w was not precise enough); within-session head motion is about 1°.
  • Angle noise attenuates β toward zero; within-subject differences in sin⁴θ are small, which magnifies this attenuation.
  • The within-subject design removes stable anatomy but not session-specific confounds that happen to co-vary with pose change.
